subject: SCIENCE
title: Light Lets Us See
objective: Distinguish sources and reflectors and explain safe seeing.
introduction: Milo turns on a lamp and the room lights up. How does light help us see the things around us?

vocabulary.definition: Energy that lets us see things.
The star that gives us light and warmth.
A dark shape made when light is blocked.

activities.instruction: Watch and listen — Milo shows how light lets us see.
activities.content: We see an object when light from a source or reflected by the object enters our eyes. Never look at the Sun, lasers, or powerful lamps.

feedback.correct: Nice work. Continue to the next step.
feedback.retry: Find the clue in Light and Sound Lab again. 💪

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: We see an object when light from a source or reflected by the object enters our eyes. Never look at the Sun, lasers, or powerful lamps.

items.prompt: Which statement about seeing is true?

options.text: Moon makes its own visible light
We see an object when light from a source or reflected by the object enters our eyes.

items.explanation: Light from a lamp or bounced off an object enters your eyes, so you can see it. The Moon only reflects light, and looking at the Sun is dangerous.

items.prompt: Which pair names an object and what it does with light?
items.explanation: A lamp makes its own light, so it is a source. Books and shirts only reflect light.

items.prompt: Which statement about light is NOT true?

options.text: Moon makes its own visible light

items.explanation: The Moon shines because it reflects sunlight — it does not make its own light. A lamp is a source, and the Moon is a reflector.

items.prompt: Why can we see a book in a lit room?

options.text: Eyes send a beam into it.
Light reflects from it into our eyes.

items.explanation: Light from the lamp bounces off the book into your eyes. Eyes do not send beams, and a book cannot make sunlight.
A book is seen when light bounces off it into your eyes — it does not make its own light. Darkness is the absence of light.
